records.question: How is end of service gratuity calculated in Qatar?
records.text: End-of-service gratuity is calculated using the worker’s last basic wage as the base amount. The gratuity must be at least three weeks of that basic wage for each full year of service, and the worker is entitled to a proportional amount for any fraction of a year worked[labour-2004:54]. For piece-work employees, the average remuneration of the three months preceding the entitlement date is used instead of the basic wage[labour-2004:72].

verdicts.claim: End-of-service gratuity is calculated using the worker’s last basic wage as the base amount.
verdicts.reason: Article 54 states the last basic wage is used as the basis for the gratuity.

verdicts.claim: The gratuity must be at least three weeks of that basic wage for each full year of service, and the worker is entitled to a proportional amount for any fraction of a year worked.
verdicts.reason: Article 54 specifies a minimum of three weeks’ wage per year and proportional payment for fractions.

verdicts.claim: For piece-work employees, the average remuneration of the three months preceding the entitlement date is used instead of the basic wage.
verdicts.reason: Article 72 states that for piece‑work employees the average remuneration of the preceding three months is used.

records.question: Can my employer refuse to pay my gratuity if I am dismissed for misconduct?
records.text: Yes, an employer may dismiss a worker and either retain the end-of-service gratuity or refuse to pay it at all. The Labour Law lists dismissal “with retention of the right to the end of service gratuity” and also “dismissal … and non-payment of the end of service gratuity” as permissible disciplinary penalties[labour-2004:59]. Moreover, the law expressly allows dismissal “without notice and payment of the end of service gratuity” in the specific misconduct cases set out in Article 61[labour-2004:61].

verdicts.claim: Yes, an employer may dismiss a worker and either retain the end-of-service gratuity or refuse to pay it at all.
verdicts.reason: Article 59 lists both dismissal with retention of gratuity and dismissal without gratuity.

verdicts.claim: The Labour Law lists dismissal “with retention of the right to the end of service gratuity” and also “dismissal … and non-payment of the end of service gratuity” as permissible disciplinary penalties.
verdicts.reason: Article 59 explicitly enumerates both options as disciplinary penalties.

verdicts.claim: Moreover, the law expressly allows dismissal “without notice and payment of the end of service gratuity” in the specific misconduct cases set out in Article 61.
verdicts.reason: Article 61 states dismissal without notice and without end‑of‑service gratuity is allowed in the specified cases.

records.question: How many days of annual leave do I get after five years with the same company?
records.text: You are entitled to at least four weeks of paid annual leave once you have completed five continuous years of service with the same employer [labour-2004:79].

records.question: Can I carry over unused annual leave to next year?
records.text: Yes, unused annual leave can be postponed to the following year, but only up to half of the employee’s entitled annual-leave period and only if the employee makes a written request for it[labour-2004:80].

verdicts.claim: Yes, unused annual leave can be postponed to the following year, but only up to half of the employee’s entitled annual-leave period and only if the employee makes a written request for it.
verdicts.reason: Article states employer may postpone up to half of annual leave to next year upon written request.

records.question: What are the working hours during Ramadan?
records.text:
During the month of Ramadan the maximum ordinary working time is limited to **thirty-six hours per week, at six hours per day**[labour-2004:73].
For workers who are minors, the limit is lower: **twenty-four hours per week, at four hours per day**[labour-2004:90].

verdicts.claim: During the month of Ramadan the maximum ordinary working time is limited to **thirty-six hours per week, at six hours per day**.
verdicts.reason: Article 73 states 36 hours/week at 6h/day during Ramadan.

verdicts.claim: For workers who are minors, the limit is lower: **twenty-four hours per week, at four hours per day**.
verdicts.reason: Article 90 states 24 hours/week at 4h/day for minors during Ramadan.

records.question: What is the maximum number of hours I can work in one day including overtime?
records.text:
The ordinary working day may be up to eight hours (six hours during Ramadan) [labour-2004:73].
If overtime is permitted, the total actual working time in a day must not exceed ten hours, unless work is required to prevent a serious loss or accident [labour-2004:74].

verdicts.claim: The ordinary working day may be up to eight hours (six hours during Ramadan).
verdicts.reason: Article 73 states 8 hours daily, 6 during Ramadan.

verdicts.claim: If overtime is permitted, the total actual working time in a day must not exceed ten hours, unless work is required to prevent a serious loss or accident.
verdicts.reason: Article 74 limits daily hours to 10 unless for serious loss/accident.

records.question: How much extra does the employer have to pay for overtime?
records.text: The employer must pay for overtime at a rate of at least the worker’s basic wage plus an additional 25 percent of that wage for the extra hours worked[labour-2004:74].

records.question: Is Friday a day off, and what am I paid if I have to work on my rest day?
records.text: Friday is the normal weekly rest day for all workers except shift workers. If a worker is required to work on that rest day, the employer must give the worker another day of rest and pay either the normal wage for a rest day or the basic wage plus an increment of at least 150 % of that wage[labour-2004:75].

verdicts.claim: Friday is the normal weekly rest day for all workers except shift workers.
verdicts.reason: Article states Friday is the usual weekly rest day for all workers except shift workers.

verdicts.claim: If a worker is required to work on that rest day, the employer must give the worker another day of rest and pay either the normal wage for a rest day or the basic wage plus an increment of at least 150 % of that wage.
verdicts.reason: Article requires compensation with another rest day and payment of either normal rest day wage or basic wage plus at least 150% increment.

records.question: Can my contract stop me from working for a competitor after I leave?

The clause is void if any of the situations listed in Article 51 occurs or if the employer terminates the employee in violation of Article 61 [labour-2004:43].

records.question: ماذا أفعل إذا حدث خلاف بيني وبين صاحب العمل على الراتب؟
records.text:
إذا وقع خلاف بينك وبين صاحب العمل بخصوص الراتب، يجب اتباع خطوات تسوية النزاع المنصوص عليها في القانون:
1. **تقديم الشكوى كتابةً إلى صاحب العمل** مع إرسال نسخة إلى الإدارة [labour-2004:129].
2. **انتظار رد صاحب العمل كتابةً** خلال أسبوع من تاريخ استلام الشكوى [labour-2004:129].
3. إذا لم يُحل النزاع برد صاحب العمل، **تسعى الإدارة إلى وساطتها** [labour-2004:129].
4. إذا لم تُفلِّح الوساطة خلال **خمسة عشر يوماً** من تاريخ رد صاحب العمل، **تحال المسألة إلى لجنة توفيق** لتقرر فيها [labour-2004:130].
5. إذا لم تُوقع كتابةً اتفاقية إحالة إلى لجنة التوفيق، **تحال المسألة إلى لجنة تحكيم** خلال خمسة عشر يوماً وتصبح التحكيم إلزاميًا [labour-2004:130].

verdicts.reason: Article 129 states workers must submit complaint in writing to employer and copy to Department.

records.question: متى يجوز فصل العامل بدون إنذار وبدون مكافأة نهاية الخدمة؟

يجوز لصاحب العمل فصل العامل دون إنذار ولا يمنحه مكافأة نهاية الخدمة في الحالات التالية:
1- إذا انتحل العامل شخصية أخرى أو ادعى جنسية غير جنسيته أو قدم وثائق أو شهادات مزورة.
2- إذا ارتكب العامل خطأً أدى إلى خسارة مادية جسيمة لصاحب العمل، بشرط أن يبلغ صاحب العمل الإدارة بالحادث خلال مدة لا تتجاوز نهاية يوم العمل التالي من علمه بوقوعه.
3- إذا خالف العامل أكثر من مرة التعليمات المكتوبة الخاصة بالحفاظ على سلامة العمال والمنشأة، رغم إنذاره كتابةً، بشرط أن تكون تلك التعليمات مكتوبة ومعلنة في مكان ظاهر.
4- إذا أخل العامل أكثر من مرة بأي من التزاماته الجوهرية المقررة في عقد العمل أو بموجب القانون، رغم توجيه إنذار كتابي إليه.
5- إذا أفشى العامل أسرار المنشأة.
6- إذا وُجد العامل أثناء ساعات العمل في حالة سكر أو تحت تأثير مخدر.
7- إذا اعتدى العامل على صاحب العمل أو المدير أو أحد رؤساء العمل أثناء العمل أو بسببه.
8- إذا تكرر اعتداء العامل على زملائه أثناء العمل رغم إنذاره كتابياً.
9- إذا تغيب العامل عن العمل بدون سبب مشروع أكثر من سبعة أيام متصلة أو خمسة عشر يوماً متقطعة خلال السنة.
10- إذا أدين العامل بحكم نهائي في جريمة ماسة بالشرف أو الأمانة.
